name: comp-107
title: Text Align Toggle
description: A single-choice row of four rounded square buttons, each showing a little paragraph-alignment glyph. Picking one makes it the only bright tile while the others fade to grey.
use: A text editor or document tool lets people switch paragraph alignment with small icon buttons.
avoid: It holds state only and has no text to act on, so it must be wired to an editable area to matter.
a11y: Each square has an aria-label and focus ring, but the chosen alignment is conveyed by colour alone. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Four light-grey rounded squares sit in a row on a near-black stage, separated by thin seams. Each holds a small white glyph of stacked lines arranged left, centred, right or justified, with the active tile a brighter white than the rest.
behaves: Clicking a square makes it the sole bright white tile and dims the others; hovering lightens a neighbour without choosing it. The row leaves a faint gap between tiles.
customise: There are no props: the four options and their icons are fixed, so swapping glyphs or adding an option means editing the file.
weight: light: Four small icon buttons with colour changes only on hover and selection.
